subject: Skylark Labs - mid-cycle metering spike / request for breakdown
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@skylark.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, billing@skylark.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected mid-month jump in token counts — need breakdown

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re well. We were reconciling November usage and noticed a ~5x spike on Nov 18 between 14:30-15:10 PST that doesn’t match any internal campaigns. Our metrics show normal traffic; vendor logs (attached) flag many repeated request_ids coming from our ingestion pipeline. Can Redwood share a per-request breakdown (request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, route) for that 40-minute window so we can map it back?

Attached: skylark_usage_export_20261120.csv and our invoice for Nov 1 for reference. We’re trying to decide whether to dispute the mid-cycle increment before the month-end invoice. Please advise next steps and any likely causes on your side (replay, batching window overlap, KV cache misses, etc.).

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Ops
Skylark Labs
attachments: skylark_usage_export_20261120.csv (csv), skylark_invoice_20261101.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@skylark.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month jump in token counts — need breakdown

Hi Ellen — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We’ve started an internal audit and I’ve looped in Ben (billing ops) and Grace (ingest telemetry) to help. Quick notes from initial triage:

- We see the same wall-clock spike in our ingestion logs for your org id (org_skylark) between 14:28–15:12 PST on Nov 18.
- Preliminary evidence points to a combination of: 1) a replayed job from your side that retried a batch, and 2) a short-lived overlap in our rolling aggregation window which double-counted a subset of sequential requests.
- The spike is concentrated on the embedding route (embed.large-v1) and a handful of text-generation calls with the "compact-claude-like" model variant.

Ben — do we have a per-request export for that window? Grace — can you pull the meter snapshot and any dedup hashes for the request_ids Ellen attached?

We’ll aim to produce a CSV with the fields Ellen requested and a short reconciliation note by EOD Wednesday. If there’s a clear double-count on our side we will propose a pro-rated credit.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Manager — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@skylark.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month jump in token counts — need breakdown

Ellen / team — attached is the export from our serving runtime for org_skylark covering 2026-11-18T14:00:00-2026-11-18T16:00:00 PST. Columns: request_id, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, server_node, dedup_hash.

Preliminary findings:
- ~2,300 request_ids show duplicate dedup_hash values that align with your attached request_ids (looks like replayed batches).
- ~1,100 request_ids were within a 30s aggregation overlap window where our streaming aggregator moved in-flight events between two worker batches — those were not de-duplicated downstream. That produced an overcount of ~1.7M tokens (embeddings-heavy).
- The rest (~600 reqs) are legitimate unique calls.

Attached: redwood_metering_snapshot_20261120.log (trimmed) and redwood_per_request_export_20261118_1428-1510.csv.

Next steps I recommend:
1) We can apply a one-time adjustment credit for the portion we confirm as double-counted on our side (we estimate ~1.7M tokens, which maps to ~$425 at your token rate).
2) For the replayed batch portion (2,300 reqs) we can provide the per-request evidence and leave it to Skylark to confirm if those were retries you triggered; if you confirm they were unintended we can discuss a separate adjustment.
3) Grace will join a short call if you want to walk through the logs.

Ben Carter
Billing Ops Lead
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_per_request_export_20261118_1428-1510.csv (csv), redwood_metering_snapshot_20261120.log (log)
From: Ellen Park <ellen@skylark.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month jump in token counts — need breakdown

Thanks Ben — and thanks for the clear split. Confirming next actions from Skylark side:

- We’ll run an internal replay audit on the 2,300 request_ids and get back with timestamps and the job id that triggered the retry by EOD Friday.
- We accept Redwood’s proposed credit for the 1.7M tokens that were double-counted due to the aggregation overlap (~$425). Please confirm how that credit will appear on our Dec invoice.
- Can we also request a short post-mortem note on what triggered the aggregation overlap and any preventive steps (config change / patch / ops runbook)? That will help Skylark’s platform team coordinate internal mitigations.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — let us know when a 20-minute call is convenient if that helps.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Ops
Skylark Labs
attachments: none
